title: Rhapsodians engagements, Jerry Green, and later bands
summary: He sat in with Armstrong unpaid, worked with the Rhapsodians at San Jacinto, lost the bass to Jerry Green until it broke, then played with Celestin, Kid Rena, Kildee and Sam Morgan.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: On the violin while I was working for them. I was working for him every Sunday night. Sometime through the week, because I know how many bands would come in town. And sometime I'd sit in there, Louis Armstrong would come in town. I'd sit in and work with him. Well, they didn't give me anything, but I imagined that they would give him all. Well, I said what it was. It didn't make anything to me. I was too glad to say that I was working with Louis Armstrong to receive anything. You understand? Yeah. And I still was with the Rhapsody and we worked from the Estores over to our... Over to our...
Did you have the San Jacinto then?

The San Jacinto. We worked from Rhapsody to San Jacinto. And we had nice engagements from jobs to jobs, you know. And there for a while. Beansie still would take out the money for his violin until it was paid for. Well, after it was paid for, they had another fella by the name of Jerry Green. And Jerry Green, he joined the band, which was a bass player, and he'd taken the violin over. And he worked with them for years and years and years. After then, the band broke up for some cause. And then the violin come back to me and I have the violin yet. But Jerry, he was working with the band. And on a picnic, some woman fell in the violin and broke it in. And after then, well, I take the violin back over and I was working with the different band. And I worked with Papa Celestan. I worked with Kid Randy. I worked with Kildee.
You heard it back? No, you can hear it. I don't know. I've heard of it. You heard of it.
No, I don't remember. I've only been around here. I started coming around here in 1937, but I didn't move here until about six and a half years ago. I see. I see.

He died, but I still work with so many different other fella. Now they have a little fella. And then I work with Andrew Morgan's brother. Sam Morgan. Sam Morgan. Sam Morgan. I work with Sam. I work with Isaiah. I work with Sam. And I work with the saxophone player. And then I work with him. And they have another little kid that is real famous, which would be our... Sam Morgan. He's a... He's a... His brother's a great drummer. And he amitated Lewis Armstrong so much.
